name: Maintain security, price and reference data
summary: Every business day the four-person investment data team makes sure the prices, exchange rates, benchmark data, security records and account structures in the book of record are complete and correct before pricing, risk, performance, reconciliations and the trading desk use them. Overnight vendor files are loaded and checked by rules, then analysts work the exceptions, challenge doubtful prices, apply overrides that the manager approves, set up new securities with a second analyst's review, and release the data by mid-morning. Failed feeds, stale prices on illiquid holdings and changes made by system releases are the usual sources of delay, and errors found later by users force republishing.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion with a vendor-hosted order management and investment book of record platform fed by several market data vendors.
baseline.notes: Rules-based price validation in the platform with exception queues; overrides, logs and checklists partly in spreadsheets; data engineering supports feeds.

unit_of_work: one business day's data validation cycle
trigger: The market close and the overnight arrival of vendor price, rate, index and reference files.
end_state: The day's prices, rates, benchmark and reference data are released to downstream systems and the manager has signed off the daily checklist.

volume.seasonality: Even through the year; heavier at month and quarter ends and on index rebalance dates, and during market stress when price exceptions multiply.

evidence.note: One cycle per Canadian business day, as in the organisation file process map and business days driver.

Three analysts in the organisation file; about 6.5 hands-on hours a business day on the daily cycle is about 1.1 to 1.2 FTE, leaving time for benchmark, pricing and risk support claimed by other workflows.
Override approvals, account approvals and daily sign-off take about 40 minutes a day.
Cost from the organisation file (NOC 21223). Feed reruns and change analysis take about 15 minutes a day on average.

systems.name: Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
IT service management and change ticketing tool
Risk analytics system (third-party factor and stress models)

steps.name: Load overnight vendor price, rate and reference files
steps.description: After the 4 p.m. close the scheduled jobs pull end-of-day prices, evaluated bond prices, exchange rates, index levels and constituents, corporate action and security reference files from the market data vendors into the investment book of record platform. The last files land in the early morning.

next.condition: next day is a business day

evidence.note: Vendor feed loading into a reference data platform is described; timings are author estimates.

steps.name: Hold the cycle over the weekend or holiday
steps.description: Friday and pre-holiday data waits until the next business morning, when the team validates it together with any weekend vendor corrections.

evidence.note: About one cycle in four or five is followed by a weekend or holiday, as in the organisation's other daily workflows.

steps.name: Run automated validation rules
steps.description: The platform runs the validation rules on every price and rate: day-over-day move against tolerance bands by asset type, prices unchanged for several days, missing or zero prices, and differences between primary and secondary vendors. It picks the gold copy price and lists the failures in an exception queue.

evidence.note: Stale, tolerance and dual control tolerance rules and gold copy selection are described in vendor documentation; RG 94 names stale, zero and out-of-tolerance prices as feed errors.

steps.name: Check every feed has arrived and loaded
steps.description: At the start of the day an analyst opens the job monitor and the load report and confirms each expected vendor file arrived with a normal record count, and checks whether last night's system release touched any data feed.

error.defect_description: A partial file is taken as complete.

next.condition: a feed is missing, late or truncated
a release changed a feed or mapping overnight

evidence.note: Failed feed share is an author estimate; release share follows about 35 IT changes a month in the organisation file, a few of which touch data feeds.

steps.name: Raise the failed feed with data engineering and the vendor
steps.description: The analyst logs a ticket, phones or emails the vendor's support desk to ask for a resend, and asks the on-call data engineer to rerun the load once the file is available.

control.basis: SOC 1 information system operations objective: processing incidents are identified, tracked and resolved on time

evidence.note: Incident tracking is a baseline SOC 1 general computer control objective.

steps.name: Validate data after an overnight release
steps.description: When a release changed a feed, mapping or validation rule, the analyst compares a sample of prices, identifiers and classifications before and after the change and confirms downstream extracts still populate. Defects go back to data engineering.

error.defect_description: A mapping defect is missed in the sample.

control.basis: SOC 1 change management objective: application changes are authorised, tested and approved before and after deployment

evidence.note: Change management is a baseline SOC 1 objective; defect share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Review price exceptions for listed and evaluated securities
steps.description: The analyst works the exception queue: for each price outside tolerance or missing, compares the primary and secondary vendor, checks for corporate actions, trading halts and news on the terminal, and decides to accept the move, switch to another approved source, or challenge the vendor.

error.defect_description: A wrong vendor price accepted because the move looked plausible.

control.basis: SOC 1 valuation objective: prices and exchange rates come from an authorised source and are updated accurately and on time; pricing policy tolerances

next.condition: one or more prices need a challenge

evidence.note: Exception review against tolerances and approved sources is described; the share of days with a challenge is an author estimate.

steps.name: Data engineer reruns or repairs the feed
steps.description: The data engineer checks the job log, reruns the load once the vendor resends, or rolls back or patches a mapping broken by a release, then tells the analyst to recheck.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a typical feed rerun.

steps.name: Challenge prices with the vendor or ask for a broker quote
steps.description: The analyst submits a price challenge through the vendor's challenge tool or email with the evidence, or asks a dealer through the traders for an indicative quote on an illiquid bond.

evidence.note: Price challenge practice is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the vendor or dealer reply
steps.description: Vendors usually answer a challenge within a few hours, either confirming or correcting the price; dealers send quotes during their trading day. Prices still in dispute are carried at the prior approved value until answered.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review stale and unpriced holdings
steps.description: The analyst runs the stale price report for holdings whose price has not changed for several days, such as thinly traded bonds, suspended shares and private placements, and decides whether the price is still fair or needs an evaluated or manual price.

error.defect_description: A stale price inside tolerance is left unchanged.

next.condition: needs a manual or evaluated price

evidence.note: Stale prices are a recognised feed error and can slip inside tolerances; shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Obtain a manual price from the portfolio manager or valuations
steps.description: For a holding with no usable vendor price, the analyst asks the portfolio manager or the valuations team for a price with its basis, such as a matrix price, last trade or broker quote, and records the evidence for audit.

error.defect_description: Manual price taken without independent support.

evidence.note: A peer pool manager documents third-party and broker evidence for fair values; the step design is an author estimate.

steps.name: Apply price overrides with reason codes
steps.description: The analyst enters each override in the book of record with the source, reason code and supporting evidence, so the gold copy reflects the corrected or manual price for all downstream users.

error.defect_description: Override keyed to the wrong security or date.

evidence.note: Failed prices are reviewed and modified in the reference data system before rules rerun.

steps.name: Approve price overrides
steps.description: The manager reviews each override against its evidence and approves it in the system, or sends it back. Overrides above a size threshold or on pool holdings get a closer look because they move unit prices.

control.basis: Pricing policy dual control: a manual price or override entered by one person is approved by another (dual control tolerance rules)

evidence.note: Dual control tolerance rules and documented approval of pricing sources are described.

steps.name: Validate exchange rates
steps.description: The analyst compares the day's exchange rates with the WM/Reuters 4 p.m. London rates and a second source, checks for missing currencies and inverted quotes, and corrects any rate before it flows to valuations and risk.

error.defect_description: Wrong rate for a minor currency passes.

control.basis: SOC 1 valuation objective: foreign exchange rates come from an authorised source

evidence.note: The WM/Reuters 4pm fix is a common reference; wrong FX rates are a known unit pricing error.

steps.name: Load and check benchmark index data
steps.description: The analyst checks index levels, returns and constituent and weight changes from the index providers against the prior day and announced changes, and loads them for risk, compliance and performance. Missing or revised index data is chased with the provider and a provisional file is used meanwhile.

error.defect_description: Constituent change missed, so benchmark weights are wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; benchmark data feeds risk and performance in the organisation file.

steps.name: Chase the index provider for missing or revised data
steps.description: The analyst contacts the index provider's client service, records the issue and loads the corrected file when it arrives, telling performance and risk which days were affected.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up new securities and update reference data
steps.description: The analyst creates securities requested by traders and portfolio managers before they trade (new issues, new listings, derivatives), filling identifiers, issuer, country, currency, classification and pricing source, and applies reference changes from corporate actions such as identifier changes, maturities and rating changes.

error.defect_description: Wrong classification, currency or pricing source on a new security.

evidence.note: New security set-up and maintenance is a SOC 1 baseline area; identifier differences across vendors are described.

steps.name: Second analyst reviews new securities and reference changes
steps.description: Another analyst checks each new or changed security record against the vendor data and the request before it is released for trading and compliance rules, and sends errors back to be fixed.

control.basis: SOC 1 objective: new securities and changes to existing securities are authorised and processed accurately (four-eyes review)

evidence.note: Return and account change shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Set up or change account structures
steps.description: When a new mandate, pool account or client portfolio change is requested, the analyst sets up the account, its hierarchy, benchmark and attributes in the book of record and the central account repository, and the manager approves it against the signed documents.

error.defect_description: Wrong benchmark or hierarchy assigned to an account.

control.basis: SOC 1 new account set-up objective and the model manager account data standards: account set-up is authenticated and approved by the manager

evidence.note: Account set-up is a SOC 1 baseline area; the model manager built a central account repository with a standard taxonomy in 2022.

steps.name: Release validated data and notify downstream teams
steps.description: The analyst completes the daily checklist, marks the day's prices and reference data as final in the book of record and emails pricing, risk, performance, reconciliations and the trading desk that data is released, listing any prices still provisional.

evidence.note: Checklists with evidence of review are recommended; release timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Publish data to downstream systems
steps.description: The released gold copy flows to the risk system, the performance system and the data warehouse in scheduled extracts, and front office screens refresh.
outputs: security and reference data in downstream systems

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Answer downstream data queries
steps.description: Through the day the analysts answer questions from unit pricing, risk, compliance and portfolio managers about particular prices, classifications or missing securities, and correct errors that users find.

evidence.note: Queries are routed to the data team in the pricing and risk workflows of this organisation; volume is an author estimate.

steps.name: Log data incidents and recurring issues
steps.description: The analyst records the day's exceptions, overrides, late feeds and user-found errors in the data quality log with cause and owner, and flags issues that keep recurring.

next.condition: recurring issue needs a feed or rule change

evidence.note: The model manager's data strategy targeted data quality governance and stewardship; the log format is an assumption.

steps.name: Analyse the recurring issue and raise a change request
steps.description: A data engineer looks at the root cause, such as a vendor field mapping, a tolerance set too tight or loose, or a missing identifier crosswalk, and raises a change request in the IT service management tool with the business case.

evidence.note: The organisation file links this process to it-change-release with change requests; effort is an author estimate.

steps.name: Manager reviews the day's data quality checklist
steps.description: Late in the day the manager reviews the checklist, the override log and open incidents, signs off the day's cycle and escalates anything that could affect a unit price or a client report.

control.basis: Evidence of daily review of pricing exceptions and overrides for the SOC 1 valuation control objective

evidence.note: The model manager's controls were tested in a SOC 1 Type 2 report from October 2021.

exceptions.name: Failed or late vendor feed
exceptions.description: A file is missing or truncated, so the analyst raises an incident, the vendor resends and data engineering reruns the load.

exceptions.name: Release changed a feed or mapping
exceptions.description: An overnight system release needs post-release checks, and a defect sends the feed back to data engineering.

exceptions.name: Price challenged with vendor or dealer
exceptions.description: At least one price is disputed and carried at the prior value until the vendor or dealer replies.

exceptions.name: Manual price needed
exceptions.description: A holding has no usable vendor price and the portfolio manager or valuations team supplies a supported price.

exceptions.name: Index data missing or revised
exceptions.description: The index provider is chased and a provisional file used until the correction arrives.

exceptions.name: Account structure change
exceptions.description: A new mandate or account change is set up and approved by the manager.

exceptions.name: Error found by a downstream user
exceptions.description: A user finds a wrong price or classification after release, and data is corrected and republished.

exceptions.name: Recurring issue needs a change request
exceptions.description: A recurring feed or rule problem is analysed by data engineering and sent to IT change.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the market close to the manager's sign-off of the day's data cycle
benchmarks.population: Daily investment data cycles at a Canadian public-sector asset manager, 2019 to 2022

evidence.note: No published benchmark; data must be released by mid-morning for pricing and risk, and the sign-off follows late in the day. Weekends and holidays add two to three days for about a quarter of cycles, consistent with the organisation's pricing, risk and reconciliation workflows.

benchmarks.unit: vendors used by large asset managers

evidence.note: Vendor marketing figure for large firms; this organisation likely used fewer, perhaps five to fifteen.
Author's estimate for a book of global equities, bonds, credit and derivatives across about $40 billion of public assets.

pain_points.description: Tolerance and stale price rules produce long exception lists on volatile days, and a stale price inside the tolerance can pass unnoticed.

evidence.note: Both describe stale and out-of-tolerance feed prices.

pain_points.description: Identifiers and classifications differ between vendors, so new security set-up and corrections are manual and need a second review.

evidence.note: Vendor identifiers differ with no universal crosswalk.

pain_points.description: Failed feeds and release side effects are found only in the morning check, which pushes back the release that pricing and risk wait for.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on the morning dependencies in the organisation's pricing and risk workflows.

pain_points.description: Override evidence, the data quality log and checklists sit in spreadsheets and email, which makes audit evidence slow to assemble.

evidence.note: Common practice in the reference period; the model manager's 2022 data strategy aimed at better governance.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Baseline SOC 1 control objectives for asset managers: new securities and changes to existing securities are authorised and processed accurately, completely and on time; valuation including securities, foreign exchange rates and derivatives is received from an authorised source; new account set-up is authenticated; processing incidents are tracked and resolved; changes to applications are authorised and tested.

sources.title: RG 94 Unit pricing: Guide to good practice
sources.publisher: Australian Securities and Investments Commission and Australian Prudential Regulation Authority
sources.supports: Commercial data feeds may include stale prices, zero amounts or daily movements outside accepted tolerances; incorrect foreign exchange rates have been applied; tolerance thresholds should be specified and checklists with evidence of review used; exception reports should cover movements outside agreed tolerances.

sources.title: About Price Validation Rules (Eagle Reference Data Center documentation)
sources.supports: Vendor documentation: user-defined validation rules applied to vendor prices (days unchanged or stale price, price tolerance and dual control tolerance rules), release logic that picks a gold copy price from the best source, and review and correction of failed prices before rules are rerun.

sources.title: From legacy silos to strategic data: fixing third-party data fragmentation in asset management
sources.supports: Large asset managers take data from 30 to 100 or more vendors with different identifiers; a stale corporate bond price passed because it sat inside the tolerance; manual cross-check spreadsheets and reconciliation effort before deadlines.

sources.title: Foreign Exchange Market Microstructure and the WM/Reuters 4pm Fix
sources.supports: The WM/Reuters 4pm London fix is a reference rate used by many institutional investors, and index trackers convert currency at the same rates as their target index; the fix window widened to five minutes from 15 February 2015.

sources.title: Public Equity Pooled Fund Financial Statements, December 2021
sources.supports: A peer public-sector pool manager's valuation framework: when broker quotes or pricing services are used, management verifies the broker or pricing service is approved for that type of instrument and documents the evidence.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: The model manager developed a data management strategy focused on quality (governance and stewardship of data) and timeliness, implemented a central repository of account information with a standard taxonomy to reduce error, and received a SOC 1 Type 2 report on controls operating from October 2021 to September 2022.

sources.title: Wages: Financial Analyst (NOC 11101), Toronto region
sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages low 27.97, median 41.60, high 73.57 (2023-2024), the base of the organisation file's analyst costs.

sources.title: Wages: Finance Director (NOC 10010), Toronto region
sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages low 41.21, median 62.37, high 96.15 (2023-2024), the base of the organisation file's manager costs.

assumptions: One case is one business day's cycle across all asset classes; the team splits the work, so price review, exchange rates, benchmark data and security set-up run in parallel in the morning (marked concurrent_with).

The custodian strikes pool net asset values with its own pricing; this workflow covers the model manager's own book of record data. Price questions raised by unit pricing and risk are worked inside those workflows by the data analyst and only general queries are modelled here.
Monthly benchmark return loading for performance is part of performance-attribution in this organisation and not repeated here.
The second-analyst review of security set-ups uses the same role id as the maker; the simulator therefore does not count it as a handoff.

Daily hands-on time of about 6.5 analyst hours, 40 manager minutes and 15 data engineer minutes is the author's estimate for a firm with about 124 external mandates, internal equity and bond strategies and derivatives overlays.

The simulator adds the hands-on time of steps that run in parallel in the morning (s15, s16, s18 alongside s07), so its median cycle of about 1.4 days overstates the real close-to-sign-off time of about 1.0 to 1.1 days.
Validation rules, tolerances and source hierarchies are taken as given; changing them goes through it-change-release.
Loaded costs per hour are taken unchanged from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading).
